doc.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01

title: Ellington, Hines and Paul's freelancing in New York with Jelly Roll Morton
summary: Barney Bigard and Simeon go off to other bands while Paul plays around New York, joins Morton's band, and records with Luis Russell.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: That's when Barney went with him.

And yeah, Barney Big Odd went with him. And Duke Ellington was looking for me for saxophone, but he couldn't find me. So instead of getting me he got Johnny Hodges. Now Simeon left and he went to Milwaukee and then back he joined Earl Hines band. So Louis Russ, I was around doing anything. I was playing around with different bands, a fellow called Wilkins, a piano player, and Edgar Dow, a piano player, Jinger Young, Richard Cheatham from Cleveland, Ohio. I played a gig with Chick Webb's band. You know, a different band. I didn't belong to any regular band, but I played around with some of the greatest around New York and I was well respected, especially a man from King Oliver's band. So finally I went, Louis Russell recommended me, and I went with Jelero Martin. Now if you notice how the read section split, Barney Big Odd went with Duke Ellington, Simeon went with Earl Hines, and I, Paul Barnes, goes with Jelero Martin. So King Oliver didn't have any band. So King Oliver was playing around just like we did with different bands around New York. So he did get a band and he did some recording. See I've never recorded with King Oliver. You never did record? No, I recorded, it's a record I recorded with Louis Russell's band. Johnny Hodges and I, we worked together. But I just can't remember the name of that number, you might get it sometime, but it was Louis Russell's band. But King Oliver went on the road and he had Dave, a fellow who played trumpet, I think that was his cousin or nephew or something.
I believe I heard it, Dave Nelson.

Yeah, Dave Nelson. Well Dave Nelson made some arrangements for King Oliver. He did arrangements. Well during that time I was playing with Jelero Martin. And that was up until 1929, or the middle of 1929, Jelero Martin had a failure. His band from New York, he had a wonderful band, one of the best I've ever played with. They wouldn't go so we got different men and it's a long story but what we went through. But that's the last I know of Jelero Martin. That was in 1929. I don't think he lived much longer after that.
He went I think down to Washington, different places.

That's right. Well when he came back I played with, that's when I worked with Wilkins. We played at Quag Long Island for about six months and we had the famous Honey Brown singing with us. The girl that was to make that picture Hallelujah, she got sick and couldn't make it and they got Ninna Mae McKinney in her place and she got fame. Honey Brown she passed off. But anyway that was in 1929. It was six months.
